topic: The Mystery of Pi in the Normal Distribution: The Gaussian Integral

sections.title: The Hook: Why Pi?
lecture_lines: The bell curve is everywhere in statistics.
But why does π appear in its formula?
Circles are absent; it seems like a mystery.
animations: Fade in Gaussian integral formula $I = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-x^2} dx$. Color: #FFFFFF.
Flash text \"Non-elementary\" below integral in color #FF0000.
Animate unit circle expanding slowly to hint at geometry. Color: #FFA500.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Gaussian Integral
lecture_lines: We need a clever trick to solve it.
animations: Display $I^2 = (\int e^{-x^2} dx) (\int e^{-y^2} dy)$ below. Color: #FFFF00.
Display $I^2 = \int \int e^{-(x^2+y^2)} dx dy$ side-by-side. Color: #00FF00.

sections.title: The Geometric Bridge: Polar Coordinates
lecture_lines: Square the integral to create a 2D plane.
Switch to polar coordinates: r, dr, and dθ.
The factor 'r' appears as the key.
animations: Animate circular region with radius r labeled. Color: #FFA500.
Display area transformation $dx dy = r dr d\theta$. Color: #00FFFF.

sections.title: The Calculation: Unveiling π
lecture_lines: Integrate over the full circular plane.
Solving this confirms the integral is √π.
animations: Display polar integral $\int_0^{2\pi} \int_0^\infty e^{-r^2} r dr d\theta$. Color: #FFFFFF.
Animate final result box showing $\sqrt{\pi}$. Color: #FFFF00.

sections.title: Synthesis and Conclusion
lecture_lines: The bell curve has rotational symmetry.
That symmetry brings π into the formula.
animations: Render 3D-like 2D Gaussian bell curve surface. Color: #00FFFF.
Rotate Gaussian surface 360 degrees to show symmetry. Color: #00FF00.
Fade in text: Calculus, Geometry, Probability linked. Color: #FFFFFF.
